title: Hepatitis B Serology: Antigen and Antibody Patterns
subject: Microbiology
preview: HBsAg generally indicates current hepatitis B infection; anti-HBs commonly indicates immunity.
quickRevision: HBsAg generally indicates current hepatitis B infection; anti-HBs commonly indicates immunity.
IgM anti-HBc supports recent acute infection in the appropriate context.
The interpretation of isolated anti-HBc requires clinical context and sometimes additional testing.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: HBsAg generally indicates current hepatitis B infection; anti-HBs commonly indicates immunity.
Anti-HBc indicates exposure to natural infection and is not induced by routine recombinant hepatitis B vaccination.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: IgM anti-HBc supports recent acute infection in the appropriate context.
The interpretation of isolated anti-HBc requires clinical context and sometimes additional testing.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Anti-HBs alone does not establish whether immunity arose from infection or vaccination without anti-HBc and history.

quiz.question: Which marker generally indicates exposure to natural hepatitis B infection?
quiz.explanation: Anti-HBc indicates exposure to natural infection and is not induced by routine recombinant hepatitis B vaccination.
